answer: Each agent posts a walnut bond, a hard-shelled stake, and every trade it settles nails a timber beam between the two bonds. When a whistleblower proves one identity fake, slashing spreads along the beams, and each linked bond loses a share in proportion to how many of its beams lead into the exposed cluster. Honest agents who trade widely lose little, while fakes that prop each other up are cross-beamed, so one exposure drains them all. Slashed stake refills the oasis bounty pool, so each extra fake adds both a bond and new beams for the cascade to burn.
